correctness.rationale: Expand T_n(b,c)=sum_k binom(n,2k)binom(2k,k)b^(n-2k)c^k. For C=v2(c)>=2B=2v2(b), normalization by b^n yields odd 2-adic unit because every central binomial factor for k>=1 is even, giving nB. For C<=2B-2, write n=2m+e and reverse index j=m-k. Divide by D=(2m+1)^e binom(2m,m)b^e c^m; the j-th normalized term is ((m)_j)^2(b^2/c)^j/(2j+e)!. Legendre gives valuation >=j(2B-C-2)+s2(j)>=1, so D is the unique odd-leading normalized term and v2(T_n)=mC+eB+s2(m). For j>=2 the falling factorial has an even factor and the term vanishes modulo four; j=1 yields m²b²/(2c) modulo four for both parity cases. At critical C=2B-1, T2=2^(2B)(u²+v), odd v can force any additional valuation r>=1 or zero; no (n,B,C)-only formula. For coprime b,c the even-b phase yields the binomial histogram across dyadic blocks and odd b gives all odd coefficients. Independently computed 2400 direct multinomial sample indices and checked these valuations/unit cases; full domain follows from symbolic term bounds.
